subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `models.providers.<id>.enabled?: boolean` contract, and what should happen when the disabled provider is the selected primary?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but adding public config surface and changing provider routing/fallback semantics requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
options.body: Add the config field and one shared eligibility helper that all provider planning, fallback, catalog, auth/status, docs, and tests use, including explicit disabled-primary semantics.

options.title: Reject provider-level disable
options.body: Keep the current model where operators remove provider blocks or edit fallback lists, avoiding another public config knob and its upgrade semantics.

options.title: Defer to provider lifecycle design
options.body: Hold this until provider enable/disable, plugin setup, auth/status, and model picker lifecycle behavior are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
recommendation.body: Add the config field and one shared eligibility helper that all provider planning, fallback, catalog, auth/status, docs, and tests use, including explicit disabled-primary semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent broad model/provider runtime and catalog refactors make this the best available owner for the shared eligibility direction.
